strings.d1.s0.name: Wat Phra Singh
strings.d1.s0.tips: Golden Lanna-style temple with the Lion Buddha; come in the morning to see the monks.
strings.d1.s1.name: Wat Chedi Luang
strings.d1.s1.tips: Giant brick stupa from 1391 (partly ruined by an earthquake); join a monk chat in the afternoon.
strings.d1.s2.name: Khao Soi Khun Yai
strings.d1.s2.tips: Northern Thailand's coconut curry noodle soup (khao soi); closes at 14:00, Sri Phum.
strings.d1.s3.name: Three Kings Monument & Lanna Folklife Museum
strings.d1.s3.tips: The three founding kings and a museum of Lanna culture (air-conditioned).
strings.d1.s4.name: Tha Phae Gate
strings.d1.s4.tips: Old city gate with pigeons; on Sundays the Walking Street starts here.
strings.d1.b0.name: SP Chicken
strings.d1.b0.tips: Skewered grilled chicken (gai yang); next to Wat Phra Singh.
strings.d1.b1.name: Wat Chiang Man
strings.d1.b1.tips: The city's oldest temple (1296); elephant stupa, a stand-in for the museum.
strings.d2.s0.name: Wat Phra That Doi Suthep
strings.d2.s0.tips: Mountain temple at 1,000 m; red songthaew 60 THB, 306-step naga staircase, golden stupa and city views, quiet in the morning.
strings.d2.s1.name: Wat Pha Lat
strings.d2.s1.tips: Hidden temple in the forest; 45-minute descent along the Monk's Trail, waterfall.
strings.d2.s2.name: Nimmanhaemin Road
strings.d2.s2.tips: Nimman: cafes, One Nimman, Think Park, boutiques.
strings.d2.s3.name: Tong Tem Toh Nimman
strings.d2.s3.tips: Northern Thai cooking; nam prik ong (pork and tomato chilli dip) and sai oua sausage, expect a queue.
strings.d2.s4.name: Maya Mall Rooftop Bar
strings.d2.s4.tips: Sunset and mountain views in Nimman; quick stop.
strings.d2.b0.name: Ristr8to Nimman
strings.d2.b1.name: Chiang Mai University Ang Kaew Lake
strings.d2.b1.tips: Campus lake with mountain views; a stand-in for Nimman.
strings.d3.s0.name: Elephant Nature Park
strings.d3.s0.tips: Sanctuary for rescued elephants; NO riding, feeding and a walk in the river, book online months ahead, vegetarian lunch included, hotel pickup 60 km.
strings.d3.s1.name: Mae Taeng River Viewpoint
strings.d3.s1.tips: Valley views on the way back; photo stop.
strings.d3.s2.name: Huen Phen
strings.d3.s2.tips: Restaurant in a 1970s Lanna house; khantoke platter, rooms full of antiques.
strings.d3.b0.name: Elephant Jungle Sanctuary
strings.d3.b1.name: Dash! Restaurant Old City
strings.d3.b1.tips: Thai food in a teak house; a stand-in for Huen Phen.
strings.d4.s0.name: Doi Inthanon Summit
strings.d4.s0.tips: Thailand's highest point at 2,565 m; 2 hours by tour or rental car, 10°C in the morning, Ang Ka moss forest trail.
strings.d4.s1.name: King & Queen Pagodas
strings.d4.s1.tips: Twin pagodas and gardens; sea of clouds.
strings.d4.s2.name: Wachirathan Waterfall
strings.d4.s3.name: Pha Dok Siew Nature Trail
strings.d4.s3.tips: 2.5 km through forest and rice terraces with a Karen village guide; coffee in Mae Klang Luang village.
strings.d4.s4.name: Mae Klang Luang Karen Village
strings.d4.s4.tips: Lunch on a terrace; village coffee and fish.
strings.d4.b0.name: Sirithan Waterfall
strings.d4.b1.name: Royal Project Inthanon Restaurant
strings.d4.b1.tips: Royal Project agricultural station; trout and strawberries.
strings.d5.s0.name: Thai Farm Cooking School
strings.d5.s0.tips: Cooking class on an organic farm; market shopping, 5 dishes (khao soi, curry paste), hotel pickup.
strings.d5.s1.name: Warorot Market Kad Luang
strings.d5.s1.tips: Locals' market; dried fruit, sai oua, Lanna fabrics, Chinatown.
strings.d5.s2.name: Wat Ket Karam & Ping River
strings.d5.s2.tips: Temple and cafes across the river; Wat Ket neighbourhood.
strings.d5.s3.name: Woo Cafe Ping River
strings.d5.s4.name: Night Bazaar Chiang Mai
strings.d5.s4.tips: Chang Khlan night market; open every night, bargain, Kalare food court.
strings.d5.b0.name: Basil Cookery School
strings.d5.b0.tips: Class in the Old City; a stand-in for the farm.
strings.d5.b1.name: Ploen Ruedee Night Market
strings.d5.b1.tips: Food courtyard with live music next to the night market.
strings.d6.s0.name: Bua Tong Sticky Waterfall
strings.d6.s0.tips: Climb the limestone 'sticky' waterfall (non-slip); 1 hour north of the city, free.
strings.d6.s1.name: Mae Kampong Village
strings.d6.s1.tips: Mountain village in the clouds; tea and coffee, wooden houses, Thai villagers.
strings.d6.s2.name: Mae Kampong Village Restaurant
strings.d6.s2.tips: Local miang (fermented tea leaves) and northern dishes.
strings.d6.s3.name: Mae Kampong Waterfall
strings.d6.s3.tips: Seven-tier waterfall in the village; walk.
strings.d6.s4.name: Flight of the Gibbon Zipline
strings.d6.s4.tips: Forest zipline (optional, expensive); or the San Kamphaeng hot springs.
strings.d6.b0.name: San Kamphaeng Hot Springs
strings.d6.b0.tips: Foot soak and boiled eggs at the hot springs; a stand-in for the zipline.
strings.d6.b1.name: Mae Kampong Coffee House
strings.d6.b1.tips: Village coffee and miang; a lighter stand-in for the restaurant.
strings.d7.theme: Sunday Walking Street and a gentle goodbye
strings.d7.s0.name: Wat Umong
strings.d7.s0.tips: Tunnel temple in the forest; monks' sayings hang in the trees.
strings.d7.s1.name: Baan Kang Wat Artists' Village
strings.d7.s1.tips: Wooden workshop village; ceramics, cafe, next to Wat Umong.
strings.d7.s2.name: Khao Soi Mae Sai
strings.d7.s3.name: Chiang Mai Airport
strings.d7.s3.tips: 15 minutes from the city by Grab; goodbye.
strings.d7.b0.name: Sunday Walking Street Ratchadamnoen
strings.d7.b0.tips: If it's Sunday: a 1 km handicraft market with temple courtyard food; book a late flight.
strings.d7.b1.name: Blue Diamond Breakfast Club
strings.note0: Grab (taxi/moto) is cheap; red songthaew 30-60 THB; scooter 250/day (licence needed). The airport is 15 minutes from the city.
strings.note1: November to February is cool and dry (best; Yi Peng lantern festival and Loy Krathong in November); March to April brings burning smoke (air pollution is bad, bring a mask), and the Songkran water fight is in April.
strings.note2: TDAC digital arrival card; Turkish citizens get 60 days visa-free. Bring cash in THB; cards work in malls.
strings.note3: Khao soi 50-70, street food 40-60, restaurant 150-250; elephant park 2,500, cooking class 1,200-1,500; round up tips.
strings.note4: Cover shoulders and knees in temples; NO elephant riding, sanctuaries only. Visit Doi Suthep in the morning and the Sunday Walking Street in the evening.
strings.note5: Coffee culture is in Nimman; Akha Ama, Ristr8to, Graph.
